event.title: At least two new federal criminal cases against companies selling controlled substances
event.proposition: US federal prosecutors bring at least two additional criminal cases, of the kind brought against Done Global, against companies (or their principals) for selling or prescribing controlled substances.
event.criterion: TRUE on the docket date on which the second qualifying case is filed. A qualifying case is a federal criminal case (indictment, information or complaint) filed after the statement date by US federal prosecutors against a company that sells or prescribes controlled substances (manufacturer, distributor, pharmacy, or telehealth or clinic prescriber), or against its principals, on charges about that sale, distribution or prescribing, as in the Done Global prosecution. Each qualifying case is a distinct docket against a different company. Civil or DEA administrative actions, settlements without charges, superseding indictments in an existing case, and the pending Done Global case do not count. FALSE at the deadline when fewer than two qualifying cases have been filed by then. Resolution source: federal court dockets (CourtListener/PACER); DOJ press releases as a secondary source.

resolution_source.name: Federal court dockets (CourtListener/PACER); DOJ press releases as a secondary source

readings: Range '2-3' read as at least 2. 'Major' read as federal criminal charges. Done Global, named next, is the reference class.

Conti et al., Nature Medicine 32(2):582-590, published online 2026-01-16 (PubMed Epub 2026 Jan 16, PMID 41545587): multicentre double-blind sham-controlled phase 2b ATTENS trial (ISRCTN82129325) of the Monarch TNS System (NeuroSigma), 150 randomized (75/75), explicitly a confirmatory test of the pilot; primary outcome (parent ADHD-RS at 4 weeks) showed no differential effect (adjusted mean difference 0.83, P=0.622).
